cells.tense: Right now the momentum has somewhere to go and is already going there.
cells.act: let the satisfaction of a finished thing land
cells.ask: Once the next ending is done, don't reach past it. Let the finished thing stand an evening and take the satisfaction in.
cells.core:
Where you are, movement comes from feeling. Intent runs in the same direction as the impulse behind it, so a thing ends, you register that it ended, and you turn toward what follows without dragging the old along. That's what this looks like running well, and it's here.

The ground is open and nothing has been built back over it yet. That's not a gap. That's the season, and it's fine to be in it. Let the last completed thing land before you start the one after — an evening where you take in what ended instead of moving past it. What you're standing in isn't stalled drive. It's the rhythm itself, and there's room in it.
cells.sheetLine: You move from feeling now, and nothing drags behind.
cells.verb: Find the rhythm that carries will and feeling the same direction
cells.place: At the clearing after a necessary ending

cells.tense: An ending has not been called yet and a structure is already being raised over it.
cells.act: gather the scattered thoughts into one line
cells.ask: Before any ending is called, sit down and pull the loose threads into one line. Then decide — this ends this week, or it doesn't. Write the call where you'll see it.
cells.core:
The rhythm has momentum in it and nowhere to put it, so whatever is ending gets held open while the coming thing is raised over the top of it. Nothing is allowed to finish. Every version of what comes after is being prepared at once, and the preparing has become the work.

What settles it isn't more movement. It's sitting down and pulling the loose threads into one line, then calling the thing: this ends Thursday, or it doesn't end. The consolidation is the direction — you already have the pieces, and the move left is putting them in order and acting on it. When one ending is allowed to land, there's ground under the drive again. That's the part a new structure can't fake.
cells.sheetLine: You're building the coming thing over an ending you won't call.
cells.verb: Find the rhythm that carries will and feeling the same direction
cells.place: At the clearing after a necessary ending

cells.tense: An ending happened and you've stayed at the door that closed.
cells.ask: Name three things that ending actually gave you — skill, time, a room, a person — and write them somewhere you'll see them. No more than three. Don't plan anything off them yet.
cells.core:
Something finished, and you haven't come forward from it. The momentum that should carry you onto the open ground is spent, and the direction that used to be obvious isn't showing itself. A chapter closed here, and you're in it like a waiting room instead of a threshold.

Pushing yourself into feeling driven again won't do it. Go back and gather what the change actually grew. Name three things the ending gave you — skill, time, a room, a person — and write them down. Not a list to plan from. Just the yield, collected. Direction returns once you've taken stock of what the last season made, and you haven't counted it yet. The open ground waits on the inventory, not on enthusiasm.
cells.sheetLine: The chapter closed. You're in the doorway, not through it.
cells.verb: Find the rhythm that carries will and feeling the same direction
cells.place: At the clearing after a necessary ending

cells.tense: The clearings keep happening and no one's name is on them.
cells.act: commit to the long build and do today's part
cells.ask: Pick what you keep returning to and showing up for anyway. Do tomorrow's part — fifteen minutes, same spot, same work. Then stop there.
cells.core:
You clear ground here. It's what you do — you let things end and make room and don't say much about it, and the endings have a way of looking like they simply occurred. The craft underneath them has no name and no audience, yours included, and it's been that way long enough that it reads as habit rather than what it is.

The work that's yours here is a long build, and it has been running underneath the clearing the whole time. Do tomorrow's part of it — fifteen minutes, same spot. Sustained making comes back into view one part at a time, and none of it is dramatic. The endings have been in service of this build. You've been the one doing it the whole stretch. Show up for it where you can see yourself doing it.
cells.sheetLine: You make the clearings. The build under them stays unnamed.
